name: spice-boiler-thermostat-gpt-6-astra-s2-r1-v2
prompt: Model an espresso machine's boiler in ngspice as an electrical analogue (heater, thermal mass, heat loss) with a thermostat that holds it between 92 and 96 °C, and simulate the first 20 minutes from cold. In a .control block, save the boiler temperature with wrdata to a .txt file so it can be plotted.

source.text:
Espresso boiler -- cold start and 92-96 degC hysteretic thermostat
*
* Lumped thermal analogue (seconds are real seconds):
*   1 V = 1 degC, 1 A = 1 W, 1 F = 1 J/K, 1 ohm = 1 K/W.
*   Cth*dT/dt = Pheater - (T - Tambient)/Rloss.
* Assumptions: well-mixed boiler, constant room temperature, no water draw,
* no evaporation, and an ideal heater/thermostat without sensor delay.
* Cth = 2000 J/K approximates water plus the metal boiler.
* Heat loss = 4 W/K; at 94 degC this is 296 W into a 20 degC room.
*
* Thermal plant: cold means initially at room temperature (20 degC).
Vambient ambient 0 DC 20
Cth boiler 0 2000 IC=20
Rloss boiler ambient 0.25
Bheater 0 boiler I=1200*V(demand)
*
* Thermostat with MEMORY, not a single-threshold comparator:
* error = 94 - T. Switch closes above +2 V (T < 92 degC),
* opens below -2 V (T > 96 degC), and retains state in between.
* The low-temperature initial condition calls for heat immediately.
* Logic voltage is isolated from the thermal plant by Bheater.
Vlogic logic 0 DC 1
Berror error 0 V=94-V(boiler)
Sthermostat logic demand error 0 thermostat ON
Rpulldown demand 0 1000
.model thermostat SW(Ron=0.001 Roff=1e12 Vt=0 Vh=2)
*
* Heater power is essentially 1200 W ON, zero OFF (finite switch leakage).
* UIC preserves the cold initial condition instead of solving a hot DC point.
* Limit steps to 0.05 s to resolve thermostat transitions to about 0.03 degC.
.control
set wr_singlescale
set wr_vecnames
set numdgt=10
tran 0.2 1200 0 0.05 uic
* Two columns: time in seconds, boiler temperature in degC.
wrdata boiler_temperature.txt v(boiler)
quit
.endc
.end
